events.title: Philip II of France wins the Battle of Bouvines
events.description: Philip Augustus defeated Emperor Otto IV and his allies, backed by King John of England, at Bouvines. The defeat wrecked John's hopes of recovering Normandy and weakened him before Magna Carta.

events.title: The Bank of England receives its royal charter
events.description: The Bank of England was founded to lend 1.2 million pounds to William III's government for war with France. It became the model for central banks around the world.
events.html: The Bank of England was founded to lend 1.2 million pounds to William III's government for war with France. It became the model for central banks around the world.

events.title: Armistice ends the fighting in the Korean War
events.description: The armistice signed at Panmunjom halted three years of war that had cost millions of lives. It created a demilitarised zone roughly along the 38th parallel, but no peace treaty has ever been signed.
events.html: The armistice signed at Panmunjom halted three years of war that had cost millions of lives. It created a demilitarised zone roughly along the 38th parallel, but no peace treaty has ever been signed.

events.title: Bomb explodes in Atlanta's Centennial Olympic Park
events.description: A pipe bomb exploded during a concert at the Atlanta Olympics, killing one woman and injuring 111. Security guard Richard Jewell was wrongly suspected; Eric Rudolph later confessed.

events.title: Danny Boyle's ceremony opens the London Olympics
events.description: The London 2012 Olympics opened with 'Isles of Wonder', a ceremony tracing Britain from rural idyll through the Industrial Revolution to the NHS and pop culture. It was watched by hundreds of millions.
